extracted.intended_audience: donors, philanthropists, charity evaluators, and GiveWell researchers
extracted.subtask_description: GiveWell's process for researching programs and implementing organizations to identify cost-effective global health and poverty alleviation grants, including program selection, organizational vetting, modeling cost-effectiveness, and post‑grant lookbacks. Focuses on where dollars go furthest and on transparency of published analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program selection: evidence-backed and cost-effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify programs that are highly evidence-backed and cost-effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “The first step in our research process is to identify programs that are highly evidence-backed and cost-effective. We start here because an organization's choice of which program to implement is one of the most important factors affecting the impact it can have.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funnel: shallow-to-intensive review prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct shallow reviews of many programs, then prioritize more intensive reviews of programs that seem most promising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Our program review process operates like a funnel. We conduct shallow reviews of a large number of programs. We prioritize more intensive reviews of the programs that seem the most promising. The more promising a program seems, the more time we spend assessing it.” Includes publishing write-ups of program investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational vetting: interviews, expert consultation, document review, site visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly vet organizations implementing promising programs by speaking with staff and other relevant experts and reviewing their documents and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “To evaluate organizations, we speak with their staff and other relevant experts and review their financial documents, monitoring data, and plans. Often, we also conduct site visits.” Used to assess whether organizations meet GiveWell’s criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of past spending and monitoring data
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine charities' historical spending patterns and monitoring data to understand their track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “We review charities' past spending and monitoring data ... to better understand their track record and expected impact.” This evidence informs confidence in implementation and historical performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forecasting future spending to model cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecast organizations' future spending to better model expected impact and cost-effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “We forecast their future spending, to better understand their track record and expected impact. This helps us more adequately model their cost-effectiveness.” Forecasts feed into grant prioritization and sizing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top Charity designation and effective funding use
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate a short list of programs/organizations as Top Charities and direct grants to those believed able to use funding most effectively at the time of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “We publish a short list of programs that meet our criteria as Top Charities and direct grants to support their work. Over time, we continue to assess the work, progress, and future plans of our Top Charities. We regularly review their funding needs and make grants from our Top Charities Fund to the top charity or charities that we believe can use the funding most effectively at the time it is granted. We publish the rationale for each such grant on our website.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding outside Top Charities based on cost-effectiveness or incubation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Make grants outside the Top Charities list when grants can incubate/scale potential top charities or when grants are cost-effective and mission-consistent even if the recipient is unlikely to become a Top Charity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “We also research and recommend grants to funding opportunities outside of our Top Charities list. Some of these grants have the goal of incubating, scaling, or getting more certainty around a potential future top charity. Other grants are made purely on the basis of expected value, regardless of the recipient’s Top Charity status. For example, when we don’t think an organization is likely to ever meet our Top Charity criteria, but the grant is cost-effective and consistent with our mission to maximize global well-being, we may still make a grant to support the organization’s work. Grants of this type are made from the All Grants Fund or through unrestricted funding.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Small discretionary grants: low-effort, high-upside opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit staff to recommend limited annual funding for small, promising opportunities without extensive evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “GiveWell enables some staff to recommend a certain amount of funding annually via 'small discretionary grants.' We believe that we can increase our expected impact by occasionally funding small, promising opportunities without investing a lot of time in evaluating them. ... these grants make up a very small portion of the total funding we direct each year.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cutting research standards: rigor, transparency, and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue research that rigorously tests conclusions, is clear and transparent, and addresses cross-cutting methodological questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of pages published: 'What we learned from red-teaming our Top Charities', 'What We Learned from Using AI to Red Team Our Research', 'How we plan to approach uncertainty in our cost-effectiveness models', 'Moral weights', 'Trying to Reproduce the RCTs Behind Our Top Charities'. Emphasis on methodological rigor and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lookbacks: monitoring, accountability, and learning from grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct systematic lookbacks (typically 2–3 years after funding) to compare original estimates with actual outcomes and to learn for future decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “We monitor progress and compare implementation to our initial expectations for all of our grants. We also regularly conduct ‘lookbacks’—systematic reviews of past grants, typically performed two to three years after the initial funding was recommended—on selected grants across our portfolio. These lookbacks serve two main purposes: Accountability: We compare and publish our original cost-effectiveness estimates and forecasts with actual program data and feedback from local stakeholders to assess the grant’s real-world impact. Learning: By identifying where our initial assumptions were too optimistic or pessimistic, we can adjust our decision-making for future grants and prioritize new research questions.” Includes published lookbacks and lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic focus: prioritize areas where dollars go furthest
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus research and funding on global health and poverty alleviation because those are areas where GiveWell has found dollars can go the furthest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “We focus on global health and poverty alleviation programs because that's where we've found dollars can go the furthest.” This programmatic focus guides which sectors are investigated and prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in publishing analyses and grant rationales
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish write-ups of program investigations and the rationale for grants to help donors decide where to give.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “We publish write-ups of these program investigations... We publish the rationale for each such grant on our website.” Transparency is a core standard applied across research, program reviews, and lookbacks.
